summary.headline: The Conservation Commission approved orders of conditions for an Eagle Scout trail project on Valley Road and an ADU on Newton Street.
summary.summary: The Conservation Commission held continued hearings on two notices of intent, approving an Order of Conditions for an Eagle Scout footbridge and trail project on Valley Road and another for a garage, accessory dwelling unit, and septic replacement on Newton Street. The commission also granted a partial Certificate of Compliance for two undeveloped parcels tied to a decades-old subdivision order on Sarsenstone Way. Additionally, members approved a Certificate of Compliance for 65C School Street following buffer zone restoration.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The commission addressed routine procedural business, including approving minutes from the June 25 meeting and voting to adjourn at the end of the evening.

topics.title: 0 Valley Road boardwalk and trail Notice of Intent
topics.summary: The commission reviewed an application for an Eagle Scout project to construct a wooden footbridge and dirt trail system on Southborough Open Land Foundation property at 0 Valley Road. The conservation agent confirmed that the project is exempt from 401 water quality certification and shared research showing modern pressure-treated wood treatments do not pose environmental toxicity risks. The commission closed the hearing and voted to issue an Order of Conditions with standard and special conditions.
key_details: Applicant: Corey Liu for an Eagle Scout project on Southborough Open Land Foundation land.
Project involves constructing a wooden boardwalk and trail system.
Commission discussed lumber types, noting pressure-treated wood is acceptable and more affordable than cedar.
A standard 10-day appeal period applies before construction can proceed.
topics.outcome: Public hearing closed and Order of Conditions approved.

topics.title: 14 Newton Street garage, ADU, and septic Notice of Intent
topics.summary: The commission considered a Notice of Intent for the construction of a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit, replacement of a septic system, and related site work at 14 Newton Street. The applicant submitted a revised plan adjusting the location of a drywell designed to infiltrate stormwater runoff from the new impervious roof area. With a state DEP file number received and no outstanding questions, the commission voted to close the hearing and issue an Order of Conditions.
key_details: Scope includes garage, accessory dwelling unit, septic replacement, and a drywell for roof runoff.
Drywell is sized to infiltrate at least 1 inch of runoff per square foot of roof.
Applicant must install erosion controls and request an inspection before starting construction.
topics.outcome: Public hearing closed and Order of Conditions approved.

topics.title: Sarsenstone Way partial Certificate of Compliance
topics.summary: The commission reviewed a request for a Certificate of Compliance for two undeveloped lots on Route 9 tied to a 1970s Order of Conditions for the Sarsenstone Way subdivision (DEP file 290-100). The owners required the certificate due to ongoing probate proceedings. Because documentation and as-built plans for the full 50-year-old subdivision were incomplete, the commission decided to issue a partial certificate covering only the two specific parcels while staff searches town records before addressing the remainder of the subdivision.
key_details: Original Order of Conditions dates back approximately 50 years (DEP # 290-100).
Affects two vacant parcels on Route 9 adjacent to Sarsenstone Way.
Property owners requested the clearance to settle an estate in probate.
Issuing the certificate does not change any existing wetland resource boundaries on the site.
topics.outcome: Partial Certificate of Compliance approved for the two undeveloped lots.

topics.title: 65C School Street Certificate of Compliance
topics.summary: The commission evaluated a request for a Certificate of Compliance for work at 65C School Street following buffer zone remediation. Earlier in the spring, an unpermitted clearing of brush occurred within the 20-foot no-touch wetland buffer. The homeowner restored the lawn, planted native shrubs, and submitted an updated as-built plan with photographic documentation demarcating the garden boundary.
key_details: Previous violation involved landscaper clearing inside the 20-foot no-touch buffer zone.
Homeowner restored the disturbed area, seeded grass, and planted native shrubs.
Edge of lawn and garden was memorialized on as-built plans to prevent future encroachment.

Issue an Order of Conditions with general and special conditions for 0 Valley Road

Issue an Order of Conditions with general and special conditions for 14 Newton Street
